reasons: No tests or test ids are checked here, so correctness is only visible by reading.
Error handling for totals exists, but the preview list is hard-coded.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of React logic, such as loading data or checking who is signed in, that a page can call.
A top-level group of related industries, such as energy or materials.
A clickable card that represents one industry on the page.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the landing page
sections.what: Brings in the page's building blocks: routing links, state, the backdrop and header, the industry and sector lists, the sign-in check, icons, and the project totals hook.
sections.why: Needed so the page can draw itself and read the data it shows.

sections.name: IndustryTile (part 1)
sections.title: Single industry tile
sections.what: Draws one clickable card for an industry, showing its name, tagline, status badge, description, and counts of stages or segments and of types. Live industries or those with project data get a red top border and a Data available or LIVE badge. Signed-out visitors are sent to login first.
sections.why: Each industry needs a consistent card, and the login redirect keeps the workspace behind sign-in.
sections.watch_out: Whether a tile looks live depends on both the industry status and the project count, so changing either one changes the look.

sections.name: IndustryTile (part 2)
sections.title: Tile footer and link
sections.what: Shows the project count and the number of stages or segments at the bottom of each tile, with a count of types when the industry has nested levels, plus an arrow icon.
sections.why: Gives a quick sense of how large each industry is before the visitor clicks.
sections.watch_out: The wording changes between stages and segments based on the structure type, so new structure types need their own label.

sections.name: Landing (part 1)
sections.title: Page state and headline numbers
sections.what: Loads project totals and works out how many records are not shown in any tile, either because they have no industry or because the industry is not catalogued. It also sets the default preview industry and prepares a helper that shows a dash while numbers load.
sections.why: Keeps the headline total honest. The page states every record, including those no tile can show.
sections.watch_out: The subtraction assumes the totals data matches the tile counts, so a mismatch shows as wrong untiled counts.

sections.name: Landing (part 2)
sections.title: Headline text, stats, and preview panel
sections.what: Shows the page title, the total projects text, a retry message on error, four or five headline stats, and a preview panel with buttons for six sample industries. Choosing a button updates the preview. An open button links to that industry.
sections.why: Gives visitors a summary of the data and a quick way to explore a sample industry.
sections.watch_out: The preview list is a fixed set of slugs, so renaming one of those industries silently removes its button.

sections.name: Landing (part 3)
sections.title: Sector sections with industry tiles
sections.what: Goes through each sector, skips any with no industries, and shows the sector name, tagline, and count, followed by a grid of tiles for its industries.
sections.why: Groups industries so visitors can scan by sector.
sections.watch_out: An industry whose sector id does not match any sector is never shown as a tile.

summary: This is the front page of the Yard, listing every industry as a tile with project counts, headline totals, and a preview panel for one industry at a time.
purpose: Gives a visitor an overview of all catalogued industries and the total number of projects in the database, and lets them open an industry workspace.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The page appears to be the entry point where people choose an industry before going deeper.
how: It loads project totals through a hook. It groups industries into sectors and shows a tile for each one. Each tile links to the industry page, or to the login page if the visitor is not signed in. Hovering or focusing a tile changes the preview panel. Totals show a dash while loading and a retry button on error.
inputs: The static industry list and sector list from the shared industries module, the signed-in state from the auth hook, and the project totals from the totals hook.
outputs: A rendered landing page with headline numbers, a preview panel, sector sections, and industry tiles with links.
risks: If the totals data does not match the tile counts, the page can show a count of records that are not in any tile. The page also relies on a fixed list of preview industries.
debug: If numbers look wrong, check the totals hook output and the industry sector assignments. If tiles are missing, check the sector id on each industry. If links send signed-in users to login, check the auth hook.
